analysis.title: A.O. Smith Corp. (AOS) 3Q26 Recap: Rising Price/Cost Headwinds and Weak Demand to Weigh on Valuation, Leaving us Cautious on AOS
key_insights: GS maintains Sell on AOS with a 12-month price target of $58 (from $55), 8.6% below the $63.49 price as of the 10/29/2026 close. The target uses 10.0x (was 9.5x) Q5-Q8 EBITDA. The higher multiple reflects North America making up a larger share of sales.

Input costs are rising. Freight and steel are each up about 15%, alongside oil-based raws and other metal components. Together they add about 5% to COGS, and management expects to exit the year at a higher run-rate.

AOS announced a 9+% price increase on residential and commercial water heaters effective early December, in line with peers. It follows a 4-7% increase implemented at the end of 2Q. GS expects benefits through 2027 but sees weak demand and channel shifts limiting price realization.

Residential water heater demand remains weak. Management reiterated 2026 industry volumes down low-single digits, versus GS at -3%. The wholesale channel is under pressure and housing is moderating, while retail has sustained momentum. Commercial is more resilient, with industry volumes expected flat this year.
3Q North America profitability benefited from a $10mn IEEPA tariff refund and about $6mn of structural cost actions, which offset the rise in input costs in the quarter.

Boilers grew 13%, led by residential share gains as competitors exit, demand for condensing products and price tailwinds. GS models 12% boiler growth in 2026 against the upwardly revised guide of +10-12%.
Leonard Valve acquisition contributes to growth, but delays in energy efficiency upgrade projects in the New York area cut the full-year revenue contribution by about $5mn to $65mn.

Water treatment outlook was lowered about 2pts to +3-4% on weaker consumer sentiment and shipment delays from production moves. Cost savings of $6-8mn a year are targeted, with about $1mn realized in 2H26.

GS models North America revenue up 4.1% in 2026 and 6.2% in 2027, largely from price with volumes flat to down. It models the 2026 adjusted EBIT margin at 23.6% and 2027 profitability roughly flat y/y.

China drove segment underperformance again, well below management expectations, on weak demand and disruption from the strategic review. AOS agreed to sell an 81% stake in China operations to CPE and expects a mid-single-digit adjusted segment EBIT margin afterward.

India continues to outperform, with a guide for double-digit local-currency sales growth this year including the Pureit acquisitions. GS models 2027 ROW sales ex-China up 7.5% with a 6.0% adjusted EBIT margin.
GS cut its estimates: 2026 adjusted EPS to $3.65 from $3.75, 2027 to $3.80 from $4.00, and 2028 to $4.15 from $4.40. Revenue estimates fell more sharply, with 2027 at $3,472mn versus $4,053mn before.
GS sees unfavorable risk/reward. Its upside case is $78 (18.8x 2027 EPS) and its downside case is $46 (13.4x 2027 EPS).
AOS has underperformed the S&P 500 by 3.0% over 3 months, 7.8% over 6 months and 13.6% over 12 months.

market_movers.rationale: Rising price/cost headwinds and weak residential demand limit revenue upside and put margins at risk. GS sees unfavorable risk/reward at the current valuation, with the target raised to $58 from $55 on a higher multiple.

sector_views.rationale: Weak residential demand, a housing slowdown and rising input costs pressure the group's price realization and operating leverage.

earnings_insights: AOS 3Q26 (reported before this note, 10/30/2026): North America profit benefited from a $10mn IEEPA tariff refund and about $6mn of structural cost savings that offset input cost inflation.
GS 2026E adjusted EPS $3.65 (new) vs $3.75 (old); 2027E $3.80 vs $4.00; 2028E $4.15 vs $4.40. These are GS estimates, not consensus.
GS 4Q26E EPS $0.84, 1Q27E $0.87, 2Q27E $1.04. 3Q26 EPS shown as $0.93. These are GS figures.
Management guides full-year boilers +10-12% (raised) and water treatment +3-4% (lowered about 2pts). India is guided to double-digit local-currency growth in 2026.

trade_ideas.description: Sell rating on AOS with a $58 12-month price target, 8.6% downside from $63.49
trade_ideas.rationale: Limited revenue upside and margin risk from price/cost headwinds and weak demand leave unfavorable risk/reward.
trade_ideas.risk: Successful new product introductions, lower raw material costs, continued commercial share gains and effective capital allocation.

risk_factors: Mid-teens increases in freight and steel and rising other input prices could outrun price realization.
Weak demand, rising competition and channel shifts may limit realization of announced price increases.
Housing and consumer confidence are moderating, putting discretionary water heater demand at risk.
Lower volumes could limit operating leverage while costs expand, putting GS's 2027 EPS estimate at risk.
Upside risks to the Sell view: new product introductions, lower raw material costs, commercial share gains and capital allocation.
geopolitical: IEEPA tariff refunds of $10mn benefited AOS 3Q North America profit.
AOS agreed to sell an 81% stake in its China operations to CPE, with China demand weak and the strategic review disrupting operations.
cross_bank_references: We also note residential and commercial water heater peers have taken similar pricing actions given the magnitude of inflation

tension_points.bull_case: AOS announced a 9+% price increase in line with peers, plus a 4-7% increase at the end of 2Q, and cost savings. Retail momentum, boiler growth of 13% and 30 new dealer partners support sales.
tension_points.bear_case: Weak residential demand, wholesale channel pressure, competition and a housing slowdown may limit price realization while costs rise about 5% of COGS, leaving revenue and margin at risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Upside risks named: successful new product introductions, a decline in raw material costs, continued commercial share gains and effective capital allocation.
